sources.title: Introducing Claude Opus 4.8
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The May 28 launch calls Opus 4.8 an upgrade that builds on Opus 4.7; its comparison is of capability benchmarks. It publishes no nominal total or active count and does not identify a separately sized base model from which a count can be inherited.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.8 - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. Exact-model specifications and the current-lineup comparison list context/output limits, pricing, thinking, effort, cutoffs, modalities and availability. Neither total nor activated-parameter counts are included. The documented 1M context is a token limit, not a parameter count.

sources.title: Claude Opus 4.8 System Card
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the original system card text from the official PDF freshly retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:50Z. Section 1 describes pretraining followed by post-training/fine-tuning, without a nominal size or separately sized named base. Section 6.6 refers to retraining from the Claude Opus 4.8 base model, which is not a count-bearing lineage disclosure. Full-text parameter/size searches and relevant sections yielded no total or active count; unrelated trillion text is in the BrowseComp URL blocklist.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5 System Card
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the official Opus 5 card freshly retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:51Z. Exact Opus 4.8 rows include Table 4.1.1.A harmless-response rates and other behavioral/capability comparisons. These are scores, not sizes; no nominal total or activated-parameter column or count was found in the card.

sources.title: Claude Opus 5.5 System Card
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the official Opus 5.5 card freshly retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:11:48Z. Table 8.14.5.A compares Opus 4.8 using Toolathlon Pass@1, Pass@3, Pass-cubed and average turns; fallback discussions identify use of Opus 4.8 without stating its size. No total or active count was found.

sources.title: Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 System Card
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the official Fable 5/Mythos 5 card freshly retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:49Z from Anthropic CDN d00db56fa754a1b115b6dd7cb2e3c342ee809620.pdf. Exact Opus 4.8 comparisons concern evaluation reruns, safety and capabilities. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning describes safeguards for another model; no nominal total or activated-parameter count for Opus 4.8 was found.

sources.title: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 System Card
sources.evidence: Independently inspected the official Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1 card freshly retrieved October 27, 2026 at 10:18:48Z. Table 8.15.5.A has exact Opus 4.8 Toolathlon scores and average turns, not parameter counts. Monitoring and fallback references also disclose no total or active size; full-text searches found no count-bearing comparison column.

sources.title: PDF support - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: All active models support PDF processing. PDF pages are converted to images and extracted text; this supports retaining pdf as a supported input format alongside text/image.

sources.title: Commercial Terms of Service
sources.evidence: API access is governed by commercial service terms; reverse engineering or duplicating the service is restricted and no intellectual-property rights are granted except as stated. Supports descriptive proprietary license classification.

sources.title: Prompting Claude Opus 4.8
sources.evidence: Exact-model guidance documents adaptive thinking, effort controls, tool use and long-horizon agentic capabilities.

sources.title: Would This Change Your Answer? Evaluating Explanations of LLM Behavior in the Wild with Counterfactual Experiments
sources.evidence: First-party interpretability research names Opus 4.8 as a predictor agent. Its activation-tool discussion concerns target models and does not establish Opus 4.8 architecture or parameter counts.

sources.title: Automated Researchers Can Mitigate Well-Characterized Alignment Failures
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 following fresh parameter and named-base searches. Section 6 has Sonnet 5 post-train an early Opus 4.8 checkpoint, but provides no size for that checkpoint or the production model. Table 1 and Appendix E identify separate Qwen, Phi, Llama, Gemma, Olmo, GLM-4-32B and Qwen2.5-72B subject models; their sizes are not Opus 4.8 specifications.

sources.title: Models.dev Claude Opus 4.8 record
sources.evidence: Followed baseline catalog link as a discovery lead; technical claims were checked against Anthropic sources.

sources.title: GLM-5.3 and the spread of advanced cyber capabilities
sources.evidence: The September 29, 2026 article explicitly states that Claude weights are not publicly released or supplied to users; the same article names Opus 4.8 among evaluated Claude models. Used only for distribution status.

sources.title: Models overview - Claude Platform Docs
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026 as a later first-party comparison-table check. The current model table reports latency, pricing, thinking, context/output limits and cutoffs, with no total or activated-parameter column. The exact Opus 4.8 page supplies its legacy comparison row, also without counts.

sources.title: Frontier Inference Margins - interactive cost model
sources.evidence: Fresh search surfaced the concrete 2.5T total / approximately 300B active Opus 4.8 lead. Opened October 27, 2026: the page explicitly labels this geometry a scenario choice and its active count highly uncertain, not a measurement. Its 5T legacy scenario comes from a reported April 9 Musk comparison predating Opus 4.8; neither is an Anthropic nominal specification. Used to resolve a lead, not to establish a catalog value.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity
sources.evidence: Opened the original research linked by the numeric lead on October 27, 2026. The revised paper models effective knowledge capacity from factual recall and explicitly presents coarse prediction bands rather than precise parameter counts. Its Opus 4.8 row leaves parameter columns blank; behavioral similarity rows are not developer-confirmed base lineage. This independent estimator does not establish Anthropic total or active specifications.

sources.title: List of large language models - numeric search lead resolution
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026 only to resolve a misleading search excerpt combining Opus 4.8 with 196B plus 1.8B and 23B active. The actual Opus 4.8 row has no count: 196B plus 1.8B belongs to Step 3.7 Flash, and 23B active belongs to MiniMax-M3. No technical catalog value is based on this secondary list.

sources.title: Sanity-checking Incompressible Knowledge Probes
sources.evidence: Opened October 27, 2026 as the numeric lead's linked methodological re-analysis. Its approximately 1.1T calculation concerns Opus 4.7 and the authors explicitly caution that sensitivity to methodology does not reveal true model counts. It offers neither an Opus 4.8 developer specification nor explicit size-preserving lineage.

sources.title: April 9, 2026 model-size comparison cited by the cost-model scenario
sources.evidence: Attempted October 27, 2026; web retrieval returned 403. The cost-model page reports the statement as a pre-Opus-4.8 comparison, so it cannot establish this exact model's count and is not used as verified evidence.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 re-audit reopened launch/specifications, independently inspected the freshly retrieved original and four later system cards, and ran exact-model searches for parameters, billion/trillion counts and named-base lineage. No developer-published nominal total or a named, publicly sized base was found. The Opus 4.8 base-checkpoint references carry no size. Resolved the 2.5T/5T cost-model and IKP leads as scenario assumptions or behavioral estimates; adjacent-table 196B and 23B claims concern other models. Null reflects absent supported nominal evidence, not a requirement for an exact tensor census.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-parameter searches and later first-party comparison-table review found no Opus 4.8 active count or activation convention. The original card and later Opus 5/5.5 and Fable/Mythos 5/5.1 cards provide evaluation scores, not active-parameter columns. The approximately 300B active numeric lead is an explicitly assumed cost-model input; 23B is a different model. No total-equals-active, non-embedding or dense/MoE inference is made.

architecture.note: Original/later cards and targeted first-party interpretability/training research did not establish exact-model architecture. Hybrid reasoning describes behavior, and SAE discussion does not establish dense/MoE topology.

modalities.note: Native text/image inputs and text output; PDF retained as supported document format processed into text/images, not a distinct native modality.

reasoning.note: Supports adaptive thinking; capability does not imply that thinking is enabled by default.

tool_call.note: Original card and exact-model prompting guidance document agentic tool use.

No size-bearing base lineage is established; third-party size estimates are not specifications. Architecture remains undisclosed. PDF inputs are processed as text and page images.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit: total and active counts remain explicitly null/undisclosed after fresh launch/specification review, original-card inspection, four later first-party comparison cards, and exact-model numeric and named-base searches. Resolved 2.5T/300B and 5T leads as third-party scenarios, IKP as behavioral capacity estimation, and 196B/23B snippets as other models. No supported nominal size or count-bearing base lineage was found. Preserve all other prior field assessments and precision.
